use_case_name: Check Files for Duplicates and Corruption

claims.content: Check files for duplicates and corruption when an original checksum or hash value is known.

goal.raw_text: Check files for duplicates and corruption when an original checksum or hash value is known.

claims.content: User
User has selected one or more files to check.
An original checksum or hash value is known for the file(s) being checked.
User selects files and invokes the check function from the file management tools interface.

trigger.raw_text: User selects files and invokes the check function from the file management tools interface.

claims.content: User accesses the File Manager Interface from the initial window of the application.
User selects one or more files to check for duplicates or corruption.
User invokes the 'Check files' utility from the set of file management tools available in the interface.
System performs byte-by-byte comparison or hash/checksum verification against known original values to detect differences or corruption.
System displays results indicating whether files are duplicate, corrupted, or match the original checksum/hash value.
If the checksum or hash value is not known, the system cannot perform corruption checking as intended.
If a proper hash function is not chosen, collision detection may become practically possible under highly improbable conditions.

If a proper hash function is not chosen, the byte to byte file comparison may be susceptible to collisions under any circumstance, even if conditions are highly improbable and very difficult or not practically possible to trigger.
The system has displayed results indicating whether the selected files are duplicates or corrupted based on comparison with known checksum or hash values.
Files identified as duplicates or corrupted are flagged for user review, enabling appropriate action such as deletion or replacement.
